title: Floquet-Sambe Bottleneck and Frequency-Selective Localization in a Driven Synthetic Spin Chain
authors: J. Cao, K. L. Zhang, R. Wang, X. Z. Zhang
abstract: We study a finite Floquet chain in which a uniform nearest-neighbor hopping coexists with a periodically rotating, \textrm{SU(2)}-dictated spin-assisted hopping profile. The resulting coupling is spatially inhomogeneous -- weakest at the chain boundaries and strongest in the bulk -- and produces a frequency-dependent Floquet-Sambe bottleneck. In the closed system, the mean inverse participation ratio (\textrm{MIPR}) of the Floquet eigenstates exhibits a striking nonmonotonic dependence on the driving frequency $ω$: the states remain extended at both low and high frequencies, but become maximally localized at an intermediate frequency. We demonstrate that this localization maximum occurs at $ω_{\mathrm{peak}}\sim μ_{-s}=\sqrt{% 2s}$, a scale controlled by the first boundary bottleneck. To connect these spectral properties to measurable transport, we construct an open-system Floquet-Sambe Green-function inverse participation ratio from the spatial density of the injected scattering state. This open-system diagnostic recovers the same nonmonotonic localization trend as its closed-system counterpart, with the peak shifted to higher frequencies by the static bandwidth and the lead self-energy. These findings establish the driven synthetic spin chain as a directly realizable, frequency-tunable platform for coherent information storage and retrieval, rooted in the interplay of Floquet-Sambe virtual channels, boundary-controlled localization, and frequency-selective transport in emerging multi-level superconducting circuit architectures.
summary: The paper analyzes a driven synthetic spin chain to understand how its localization properties depend on the external driving frequency ($\omega$). It finds that the system exhibits maximal state localization at an intermediate frequency ($\omega_{	ext{peak}}$), dictated by boundary coupling strengths. This establishes the model as a promising, tunable platform for controlling quantum information storage and retrieval in superconducting circuits.
main_problem: The study investigates how driving a synthetic spin chain with spatially inhomogeneous coupling leads to frequency-dependent localization phenomena, termed the Floquet-Sambe bottleneck.
main_result: The system exhibits maximal state localization at an intermediate driving frequency ($\omega_{	ext{peak}}$), which is controlled by the weakest boundary hopping scale. This nonmonotonic behavior is robustly observed in both closed and open-system diagnostics.
method: The analysis employs Floquet theory, transforming the time-dependent problem into a static eigenvalue problem in an enlarged space, and utilizes Inverse Participation Ratios (IPR) to quantify localization.
model_or_system: The model is a finite Floquet chain combining uniform hopping with a periodically rotating, SU(2)-dictated spin-assisted hopping profile. The resulting coupling strength varies spatially, being weakest at the boundaries.
key_observables: Mean Inverse Participation Ratio (MIPR) for closed systems and the energy-integrated IPR ($	ext{IPRG}(\omega)$) for open-system transport diagnostics.
important_parameters: Driving frequency ($\omega$), boundary bottleneck scale ($\mu_{-s} \sim \sqrt{2s}$), and the ratio of hopping to driving strength ($\eta_j = \mu_j / \omega$).
main_assumptions: The analysis involves truncating the Fourier components for numerical simulation, and comparing limits such as $\omega 	o 0$ (adiabatic) and $\omega 	o \infty$ (high-frequency expansion).
figures_summary: Figures show the nonmonotonic MIPR profile peaking at $\omega_{	ext{peak}}$ for varying spin dimensions ($s$), and similarly demonstrate the peak in the open-system IPR ($	ext{IPRG}(\omega)$) shifting with $s$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the system across different frequency regimes: low-$\omega$ (PST revival), intermediate $\omega$ (localization maximum at $\omega_{	ext{peak}}$ due to boundary bottleneck), and high-$\omega$ (effective tight-binding behavior via Magnus expansion).
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, tunable mechanism—the Floquet-Sambe bottleneck—to engineer quantum transport properties by controlling the driving frequency, which is highly relevant for superconducting circuit architectures.

(b)-(d) Spatial proﬁles of three selected eigenstates: the ground state (λ = 1), the middle state (λ = s + 1), and the highest state (λ = 2s + 1). These static-limit results establish the spectral baseline for comparison with the periodically driven case. Parameters: κ = 1, s = 20, and Qλ,j = |qλ,j|2.

FIG. 2. Frequency dependence of residual PST character in the low-frequency regime. Each column corresponds to a typical driving frequency: ω = 0.1 [panels (a1-a2)], ω = 0.08 [panels (b1-b2)], and ω = 0.07 [panels (c1-c2)]. Top row: Space-time proﬁle Pj(τ) = |⟨j|Ψ(τ)⟩|2 showing the propagation of an initially boundary-localized state (site state localized at j = −20). FIG. 3. Floquet quasi-spectrum (blue star) compared with the eﬀective static tight-binding spectrum governed by Heﬀ,1 (red square) for driving frequencies (a) ω = 20, (b) ω = 50, and (c) ω = 100. With increasing ω, the Floquet spectrum converges to the cosine band of the eﬀective uniform tight-binding chain, consistent with the high-frequency expansion. Other parameters: κ = 1 and s = 20.

FIG. 4. Bloch-like oscillation dynamics and spectral structure at a speciﬁc driving frequency. (a) Space-time proﬁle Pj(τ) = |⟨j|Ψ(τ)⟩|2, showing the propagation of an initial state along the spin chain. The wavepacket exhibits pronounced Bloch-like oscillation, with the probability density oscillating over multiple cycles. (b) Instantaneous eigenvalues Eλ at τ = 0 (red) and the overlap Pλ = |⟨φλ|Ψ(0)⟩|2 of the initial state with each eigenstate (blue). The initial state populates exclusively a narrow band of central eigenstates with approximately equal energy spacing, which governs the coherent revival dynamics observed in panel (a). Parameters: ω = 9, κ = 1, and s = 20.

FIG. 6. Energy-integrated IPR [IPRG(ω)], as a function of driving frequency ω for three spin quantum numbers s = 10 (red), s = 15 (blue), and s = 20 (black), the green arrow de- notes the position of ωc ≈7.1, 8.2, and 9.3, respectively. The energy range E ∈[−2, 2] is discretized using a uniform mesh with ∆E = 4/150. The peak position increase monotoni- cally with s, which is consistent with the theoretical analysis presented in the main text. Other parameters: κ = 1 and M = 50, and s = 20.
